text:
sara: Quick follow-up on the crediting + fanout contract refactor I sketched. posted the draft in the RFC repo: https://git.redwood/rfcs/crediting-fanout
mike: Saw it - nice clarity. primary question for me: do we emit per-token 'credit' events from the serving runtime, or emit per-request aggregates and let the ledger split later?
anya: per-token gives exactness for audits but kills throughput unless we batch aggressively. per-request is cheap but makes provenance harder for reconciliation.
patrick: Agreed. Also think about SLA windows — realtime billing needs lower latency, audits can tolerate replay cost.
sara: My proposal leans toward hybrid: runtime emits compacted oplog entries with a token-range fingerprint and rough counts, then a downstream finalizer expands to per-token attribution only when requested by an audit/replay.
mike: Hybrid sounds promising. Concern: how do we guarantee deterministic finalization? if finalizer replays over different inputs we could diverge.
anya: determinism via canonical fingerprint + stable sort key. we already do something similar for ingestion handshakes. Example event shape I pasted in the RFC:
```
{ "request_id": "r_123", "tenant": "acme", "fingerprint": "fp:sha256(...)", "tokens": 321, "buckets": [{"model":"redwood-7b","count":321}], "compact": true }
```
patrick: That helps. Also add `source_seq` coming from serving so we can check idempotency on finalizer.
sara: Good call. We should pick a shard key that keeps a tenant's events colocated but avoids hot tenants — maybe hash(tenant) mod N + time-window bucket.
mike: What about late arrivals? We need a watermark policy + TTL after which we don't expand. For billing/legal we probably need a long grace period, but for operational cost shorter.
anya: Yes — suggest: 7-day full fidelity window, 90-day compact-only window. audits older than 7d can still run but will reconstruct from compacts (higher cost/less resolution).
sara: Also thinking about replay safety: finalizer should write provenance pointers back to the ledger so downstream consumers can find the expansion artifact. That way audits don't have to re-run the heavy expansion every time.
patrick: +1. That solves repeated-expansion cost. Also add a checksum field to final artifacts so audit job can assert binary equivalence vs re-expansion.
mike: Operational note: make the finalizer idempotent and lease-protected. If a finalizer crashes mid-expansion we must be able to resume without double-charging.
sara: i'll add pseudo-flow to the RFC: (1) runtime writes compact event to fanout topic; (2) fanout replicates to tenant shards; (3) finalizer claims lease, expands if within fidelity window, writes expansion artifact to archive + ledger pointer; (4) billing reconciler reads final artifacts.
anya: small implementation detail: make the 'compact' events include a minimal provenance envelope (model version, prompt hash, sampling seed?) so expansion can be deterministic.
patrick: can we add a fast-path for small requests (tokens < 16) where runtime emits expanded events directly to save a finalizer roundtrip?
mike: yes but keep that bounded — otherwise hot small-req tenants become flood risks. rate-limit expanded direct emits per-tenant.
sara: sounds like we have consensus on hybrid + artifact caching + TTL windows. action items:
- sara: update RFC with shard key proposal + pseudo-flow (today)
- mike: prototype finalizer lease logic + resume idempotency (next week)
- anya: run cost estimate for full-fidelity expansion vs compact-only (end of week)
- patrick: add checksum + artifact pointer schema to ledger contract (tomorrow)

sara: any objections? if none i'll mark RFC as 'follow-up: implementation plan' and schedule a short sync.
anya: no objections from me :+1:
mike: no objections, go ahead.
patrick: fine by me.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: rfc/crediting-fanout update -> canary tomorrow 03:00 UTC :rocket:
